---
title: "Encoding ancient Greek musical notation"
---


- two systems (vocal, instrumental)
- semantic ambiguity in Unicode: graphically ambiguous vocal, instrumental code points not distinguished
- encoding of Greek musical notation defined in Holy Cross thesis of Zach Sowerby (HC '19) uses URNs to identify musical notation

[This table summarizes](https://github.com/neelsmith/mousike/blob/main/reference/sowerby_system.cex), based on [this work by Zach](https://github.com/zachsowerby/agm_test/blob/main/AGM_python/musical_Unicode_Pitch.csv)


- All in NS `urn:cite2:zst:gvn:`, assumed in short forms used in this package
- two collections: `gvn` and `gin`.
- two tiers of note citation: base note and sharpenings of it.

Examples: `gvn:1.1` (vocal E) and `gvn:1.2.` (vocal first sharp of E)

both in vocal notation (`gvn`); both refere to same base pitch (`gvn:1`); distinguish E (`gvn:1.1`) from first sharp of E (`gvn:1.2`).
